verdict.best_for: A founder who will stay on the Wasp framework and wants a free, MIT, batteries-included SaaS base today: verified email auth, Stripe/LemonSqueezy/Polar billing, an admin dashboard with analytics, S3 uploads, a PgBoss cron job and an AI demo, plus a separate Astro docs/blog site.
verdict.weak_for: Anyone who needs mainstream node tooling (no npm run dev/build), a non-Wasp framework, i18n/multi-tenancy/teams, or a test suite that runs offline - none of that is in the code, and the framework choice is the whole app.
verdict.swap_burden: heavy - the repo IS a Wasp spec; queries, actions, routes, auth, jobs and deploy are framework primitives, so leaving Wasp means a full rewrite, while swapping the individual services (payments, email, storage, analytics) is genuinely cheap because they are thin, isolated modules.

tests.notes: 4 Playwright specs (authRedirectTests, demoAppTests, landingPageTests, pricingPageTests) in template/e2e-tests with baseURL localhost:3000 and a webServer that runs the Wasp app itself. vitest 4.1.9 IS a devDependency of template/app but the template ships ZERO unit/component test files. e2e cannot run without real STRIPE_* test keys, an OPENAI_API_KEY and the Stripe CLI listening on /payments-webhook, so it is not a local-only smoke suite.

templates.name: Next-js-Boilerplate
templates.canonical_notes: auth=clerk -> swap to better-auth; no docker/compose (Coolify prefers a Dockerfile or nixpacks)

verdict.best_for: A new Next.js 16 App Router product that needs the boring plumbing done and nothing else: real auth with hosted UI, Postgres+Drizzle with migrations wired into the build, two-locale i18n, a full unit/integration/e2e/Storybook harness and a CI pipeline that works on day one.
verdict.weak_for: Anything SaaS-shaped beyond accounts - no billing/Stripe, no teams, roles or permissions, no email, uploads, admin panel, analytics or API keys; the paid Pro/Plus sibling kits are where those live.
verdict.swap_burden: light - no Dockerfile and almost no proprietary lock-in (Clerk is the only deep one, 3-5 days to replace), so the real work is deleting the sponsor/demo surface and adding your own UI kit and features.

tests.notes: unit_files = src/templates/BaseTemplate.test.tsx + src/utils/Helpers.test.ts. vitest.config.ts defines two projects: 'unit' (node env, src/**/*.test.ts) and 'ui' (*.test.tsx + src/hooks/**/*.test.ts in headless chromium via vitest browser mode + Playwright). e2e_files = tests/e2e/{Counter,I18n,Sanity.check,Visual}.e2e.ts; there is also 1 integration file (tests/integration/Counter.integ.ts) which Playwright, not vitest, runs (testMatch '*.(integ|e2e).ts'). Storybook 10 + 1 story file, tested with `npm run storybook:test`. CI.yml jobs: build, static (commitlint + next typegen + oxlint + knip + i18n-check), unit (+Codecov), storybook, e2e (+Chromatic visual regression; chromium locally, chromium+firefox in CI). Sanity.check.e2e.ts is consumed by Checkly, not by CI. package.json scripts: test, test:e2e, storybook:test, check:types, check:deps, check:i18n, lint.

verdict.best_for: A Python-team SaaS starter that already ships production-shaped plumbing — JWT auth with password recovery, admin user management, Postgres+SQLModel+Alembic migrations, typed auto-generated TS client, pytest+Playwright CI and Docker/Traefik deploy — so a new API+SPA product can start from login/admin/migrations on day one.
verdict.weak_for: Anything needing multi-tenancy, teams/orgs, billing, i18n/RTL, file uploads, background jobs or a real Next.js/SSR frontend — none of those exist here, and the only domain model is a placeholder Item; it is also pinned to Python 3.14 and bleeding-edge JS majors.
verdict.swap_burden: medium — auth is hand-rolled JWT (no library to rip out, but no OAuth/orgs either), the SwiftUI-free stack is otherwise standard; the real work is deleting the Item demo domain, rewriting the FastAPI-Cloud/Traefik deploy glue, and re-exporting the React Email templates after any copy change.

tests.notes: Backend: pytest 5 test modules (tests/api/routes/test_{items,login,private,users}.py + tests/crud/test_user.py) plus conftest.py and tests/utils; CI enforces `coverage report --fail-under=90` and uploads smokeshow HTML coverage. Frontend: Playwright only (6 spec files + tests/auth.setup.ts storage-state project, chromium/firefox/webkit projects) — no vitest/jest unit layer, so there is no frontend unit test safety net. E2E specs drive the real stack through Mailpit (frontend/tests/utils/mailpit.ts) for password-reset tokens. Lint/type CI: ruff+mypy+ty (backend), biome (frontend), pre-commit with zizmor. CI needs Docker (db + mailpit) and `scripts/prestart.sh` before tests.

deploy.build_cmd: bun run --filter frontend build (root) / in Docker: backend/Dockerfile stage 1 runs `bun install` + `bun run build` in frontend, output lands in backend/app/frontend
deploy.start_cmd: backend image CMD: fastapi run --workers 4 ; compose.override dev command: fastapi dev --host 0.0.0.0

templates.name: Next-Elite
templates.boot_tests: not run (playwright suite would need browser downloads)

verdict.best_for: A frontend-first Next.js 16 SaaS/admin shell where the backend already exists: auth pages, RBAC role slots, sidebar dashboards, 42 UI primitives and a 6-locale RTL-aware i18n layer are done and ready to point at your own REST/GraphQL API.
verdict.weak_for: Anything that must store data itself - there is no database, ORM, migrations, billing, email, uploads, jobs or search code, and Better Auth has no adapter wired, so accounts and sessions must be finished before the demo credentials mean anything.
verdict.swap_burden: light - nothing paid is load-bearing (Sentry and Vercel Analytics are DSN-gated and deletable) and branding/SEO is centralised in src/features/site/site.config.json plus messages/

tests.notes: Unit/component tests are colocated as *.test.ts(x): button, card, demo/accounts, rbac/roles, schemas/login, schemas/register, libs/env, libs/utils, plus tests/auth/authorization.test.ts, tests/auth/roles.test.ts, tests/i18n/routing.test.ts (11 files). jsdom + @testing-library/react, shared renderWithProviders helper in tests/utils/render.tsx, config/vitest.config.ts forces SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION=true. E2E is one spec, e2e/home.spec.ts (home title, source-code link, /api/health json, /login field ids), with a self-started web server on 127.0.0.1:6767 - dev locally across chromium+firefox+webkit, production start:standalone + chromium only in CI. check.yml runs typecheck -> lint (oxlint + oxfmt) -> knip -> vitest -> build.

verdict.best_for: A production-shaped single-tenant web app that needs real auth (password + 2FA + passkeys + GitHub SSO), RBAC, file uploads, transactional email and a SQLite database, deployed as your own Docker container.
verdict.weak_for: Multi-tenant SaaS that needs billing, i18n/RTL, Postgres scale-out, background jobs or edge/serverless hosting - none of that exists here, and the Fly.io + LiteFS + Tigris coupling is opinionated.
verdict.swap_burden: heavy - auth is hand-rolled and correct but is entwined with sessions/verification/permissions, and hosting is woven through the Dockerfile, litefs.yml, fly.toml, CI, the rate limiter (fly-client-ip) and storage (AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3), so dropping Fly means rewriting the deploy layer plus the storage signature code.

tests.notes: Vitest config lives in vite.config.ts (include ./app/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}, globalSetup tests/setup/global-setup.ts, v8 coverage). 7 unit test files (app/**/*.test.*): auth.server, headers.server, misc.error-message, misc.use-double-check, sentry-event-filters, routes/_auth/auth.$provider/callback, routes/users/$username/index. 8 Playwright specs in tests/e2e (2fa, error-boundary, note-images, notes, onboarding, passkey, search, settings-profile) with image fixtures and test helpers. tests/setup/setup-test-env.ts loads .env via dotenv and makes console.error/console.warn THROW. CI is a single workflow with 5 jobs (lint, typecheck, vitest, playwright, container) plus a deploy job; each job copies .env.example to .env and runs prisma migrate deploy first. scripts.validate = run-p test lint typecheck test:e2e:run.

verdict.best_for: A mobile-first AI photo logger: it is a genuinely functional product skeleton (anonymous onboarding -> AI-generated calorie/macro targets -> camera scan -> daily log with streaks and account deletion) for a consumer health, fitness or any-photo-logged app on iOS/Android.
verdict.weak_for: Anything web-first, self-hosted or needing maintenance: the API exists only as Expo Router server routes aimed at EAS Hosting, it cannot run until four paid vendor accounts (Clerk, Neon, Trigger.dev, ImageKit) exist, and it is explicitly a course build — PLAN.md says 'This is a tutorial/course build', one author wrote all 10 commits over 10 days (2026-07-25 to 2026-08-04), there is no CI, no issue history and a single self-check file instead of a test suite.
verdict.swap_burden: heavy — four coupled vendors (Clerk auth, Neon Postgres + Drizzle, Trigger.dev jobs + Realtime, ImageKit storage) are wired through routes, tasks and screens, and with no CI or tests nothing will catch a botched swap.

tests.notes: The only test-like artifact is src/lib/plan.check.ts — a self-check script run with `node --experimental-strip-types src/lib/plan.check.ts` (node:assert/strict, asserts the Mifflin-St Jeor math, the AI-plan validator and the zod trust boundary); tsconfig explicitly excludes '**/*.check.ts'. No jest/vitest/playwright/testing-library in dependencies, no .github directory, and PLAN.md A8 states the project intentionally has 'no staging, no CI/CD'.

stripe.note: a processor is a service, not a code lock-in: keep it, or replace with the client's local method

verdict.best_for: A business that needs a production-grade AI-agent web app (RAG chat, subscriptions, multi-tenant orgs, admin panel) as GENERATED SOURCE they own - pick your flags, get a real FastAPI+Next.js codebase with 28 migrations, Docker/k8s, Stripe billing and i18n already wired.
verdict.weak_for: Anyone wanting a repo to clone-and-run or a non-AI SaaS: this is a generator (you must install the CLI or use the web configurator to get an app at all), and every generated project carries the AI-agent assumption (Pydantic AI/LangChain) plus a 55-page, 190-component frontend you will spend real time deleting.
verdict.swap_burden: medium - vendors are all feature-flagged with code branches already written (Stripe->Paddle/LS/Polar, OpenAI->Anthropic/Google, Milvus->pgvector, LangSmith/Sentry off by default), but the generated app is 95k LOC across two languages and the frontend's 190 components + 2-locale copy are hand-rewriting, not a config flip.

tests.notes: Two layers. REPO (generator): tests/ with 21 test_*.py (test_generator, test_template_integration, test_upgrade_*, test_cli). GENERATED project: 34 backend tests (backend/tests/ incl. test_tenant_isolation, test_rbac_teams, test_ssrf, test_stripe_seats) and frontend vitest (only 1 unit test file found: components/ui/button.test.tsx) + 3 playwright e2e specs + auth.setup.ts. Generated jinja CI runs ruff + ty + pytest (with postgres service) + pip-audit + Trivy, frontend lint/type-check/vitest/playwright. Repo README claims `coverage-100%` badge and pyproject sets fail_under=100 for the generated app.

verdict.best_for: A tutorial-grade but genuinely complete Expo/React Native reference for an AI trip-planner or similar AI-generation mobile product — real auth, real Postgres schema, a durable Inngest generation pipeline, streaming chat assistant and image pipeline — best used as a working starting point to rebuild the same feature set rather than as maintained infrastructure.
verdict.weak_for: Anything expecting production maturity: it is a 6-day, single-author, 16-commit tutorial build with no tests, no CI, no Docker/migrations, hardcoded dev-mode Inngest, client-side-only route gating, no admin/roles, no i18n, no payments and no email — and it cannot run in Expo Go or a container, so a native toolchain (or a new EAS setup) is a prerequisite for even the first screen.
verdict.swap_burden: medium — Clerk, Neon, Inngest, ImageKit, Unsplash and Sentry are all isolated behind thin single-purpose modules (src/lib/auth.ts, src/db/index.ts + drizzle, src/inngest/*, src/lib/images.ts, src/lib/env.ts), so each swap is small, but the mobile-only toolchain, hardcoded isDev Inngest and client-side route protection must be fixed before anything is deployable.

tests.notes: Zero test files at any depth (tree grep for test/spec/__tests__/vitest/jest/playwright returns nothing) and no .github directory at all — gh api repos/.../contents/.github returns 404, so the repo has no CI, no issue templates, no CodeRabbit config despite the README advertising 'AI Code Review with CodeRabbit'. The only JSON under .claude/skills/*/evals/ are Claude Code skill evaluation specs, not application tests.
